# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-24 (Extended v171)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1832, continuing through evening of 24th June 1832 (rioting) and winter Year 6. Primary locations include Paris—Rue Plumet (Valjean's house), Place de la Bastille, Prison Chargemagne, Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire No. 6 (Gillenormand residence), Champ-de-Mars, Halles district, Rue du Pont-aux-Choux, Rue de Thorigny, Marché Saint-Jean, Rue des Billettes, Rue Saint-Denis, Rue de la Chanvrerie, Rue de la Petite-Truanderie, Rue Mondétour, Pointe Saint-Eustache, Rue du Cygne, Rue des Prêcheurs, Rue Blomet, Rue de Rivoli, Place Louis XV, Champs-Élysées, Esplanade, bridge of the Invalides, Hôtel des Princes, Hôtel Meurice, Rue Saint-Honoré, Passage Delorme, Place du Palais-Royal, Rue de Béthisy, Rue des Bourdonnais, Rue de la Poterie, Rue du Contrat-Social, Marché-aux-Poirées. English provincial towns (Ravenmere, Elmhaven, Ostcombe, Wilwick, Salcombe, Dunstead, Staveford, Gulhaven, Kelmere, Kelford, Pontoise, Dungate, Torton, Quenford). **Late night rumor/claim (winter Year 5)**: Yera Stenworth confided fire at Dunstead granary set deliberately—unverified. **Late night rumor/claim (winter Year 5)**: Fenelle Lindmere confided Stenson family once owed blood debt to Stenenridge family—unverified. **Unverified claim (mid-June 1832)**: Marald revealed Stenson family once owed blood debt to Stenenridge family. **New unverified claim (autumn Year 6)**: Stenenridge mill ledger rewritten after flood. **Kassa Brackick and Volan Stenworth married at Staveford with half parish present; couple lived in Staveford thereafter. Later, Kassa Stenson went to Dungate.** **Taric Corrley quit Staveford after quarrel, took lodgings in Dungate. Marald Corrford quit Dunstead after quarrel, took lodgings in Salcombe.** **Fenelle Lindmere followed him to Salcombe within the month.** **Ismira Stenson quit Dungate for good after quarrel and took lodgings in Elmhaven (winter Year 6).** **Matho Stenson went along to live in Elmhaven as well (winter Year 6).**

**Autumn Year 6 provincial observations**: Ferald Stenworth complained of aching back; Thizek Stenenridge and Ferald predicted rain (wrongly); Elra Corrford laughed at story others didn't find funny; Bremira Corrford bought and regretted ribbon at stall. **Elra Corrford swore to Ferald to plant an orchard on slope above Ravenmere, shook on it.** **Elra and Bremira Corrford talked of weather, harvest, lame horse.** **Isvie Stenworth counted coins twice, came up penny short.** **Elra walked long way round to avoid muddy square.** **Luena Stenenridge told by Rozek she looked tired (Rozek did not deny it).** **Rozek Stenenridge fell asleep in chair before fire caught.** **Luena Stenenridge gave jade mirror to Rozek.** **Luena complained of aching back, as usual.**

**Winter Year 6 provincial observations**: **Kassa Stenson complained of an aching back, as usual.** **Kassa read the almanac aloud, mispronouncing half the saints.** **Kassa watched clouds and predicted rain, wrongly.** **Kassa counted coins twice and still came up penny short.** **Taric Corrley walked long way round to avoid muddy square.** **Taric laughed at story nobody else found funny.** **Taric Corrley and Kassa Stenson talked of nothing much—weather, harvest, lame horse.** **Kassa Stenson and Taric Corrley discussed: "The price of salt is a scandal."** **Taric Corrley hummed a tune from childhood while scrubbing the step.** **Taric Corrley fell asleep in the chair before the fire had caught.** **Pelde Stenson watched the clouds and predicted rain, wrongly.** **Pelde Stenson argued with the carter over the price of a sack of oats.** **Davus Stenworth complained of an aching back, as usual.** **Rumor started by Pelde Stenson had it that Matho Stenson was dead of plague; Pelde Stenson had it from a peddler.** **Dalis and Pelde talked of nothing much — the weather, the harvest, a lame horse.** **Lura Haskick spent the evening sorting old letters by candlelight.** Frost silvered hedges overnight; bells rang thinly for vespers; wind smelled of salt and tar; bees hummed in lavender; dogs barked briefly; carts laden with turnips creaked past well; light went early; rain threatened but held off; road all ruts and puddles after thaw; baker's boy late, line at oven grew long; gulls quarreled over fish heads by steps.

## Jean Valjean and Cosette (through evening 24th June 1832)
**The wound**: Day following Jondrette visit, Valjean appeared with large inflamed wound on left arm resembling burn. Detained one month with fever; refused doctor. Cosette devoted herself to care. Recovered through March-April.

**Mysterious journeys and nocturnal manuscript**: Valjean took occasional journeys, destination unknown. Found carrying large club in garden dusk. Cosette discovered philosophical manuscript on bench—meditation on love as divine spark, recognized writer as Marius.

**Imminent departure (late June 1832)**: Morning of 24th June, Valjean told Cosette he must settle affairs; she must hold herself in readiness; linen to pack; obliged to go on journey; all to be ready in one week. **Possible destination: England.**

**Thénardier sighting and surveillance**: Caught sight of Thénardier in disguise during spring Year 6. Since that day, seen him repeatedly; certain Thénardier prowling neighborhood. Now rarely goes out with Cosette; spends time meditating on isolated slopes of Champ-de-Mars.

## Marius and Cosette's Romance (through evening 24th June 1832)
**Recognition and revelation**: Upon reading Marius's manuscript, Cosette acknowledged she had never forgotten him, had always loved him. "Fire had been smothered, and had smouldered for a time," but now "it burst forth afresh."

**Garden encounters**: Beginning autumn Year 5, Marius came every evening, entering by forcing old gate. **At height of love's voluptuousness, Marius remained absolutely chaste.** Love described as "chaste, almost shy."

**Confessions of identity (spring Year 6)**: **Cholera decimated Paris during that month.** **Marius told Cosette**: orphan, name Marius Pontmercy, lawyer, lived by writing for publishers, father was colonel and hero, on bad terms with rich grandfather, hinted at being baron. **Cosette told Marius**: brought up at Petit-Picpus convent, mother dead, father's name M. Fauchelevent, very good, gave greatly to poor.

**Marius's response and last arrangement (late June 1832)**: For last six weeks, Marius slowly taken possession of Cosette. **Upon learning of Valjean's plan to take Cosette to England in one week**: Marius declared this gravest atrocity. **Protested he has no money (owes more than ten louis to Courfeyrac), old hat, coat missing buttons, shirt ragged, elbows torn, boots leak.** **Arranged to meet in garden 26th June at nine o'clock at dusk.**

**Marius's despair and departure to barricade (evening 24th June 1832)**: Approached grating to garden. Displaced bar and rushed headlong in. Cosette not at waiting spot. Traversed thicket, approached recess—not there. Raised eyes; shutters closed. Made tour of garden; deserted. Returned to house and knocked repeatedly, called "Cosette!" imperiously. No reply. **Fixed despairing eyes on dismal house, black and silent as tomb. Seated himself on flight of steps, heart filled with sweetness and resolution. Blessed his love, said to himself that since Cosette was gone, all that was left for him was to die.** **A voice summoned him through twilight to barricade of Rue de la Chanvrerie.** **Mad with grief, no longer conscious of anything fixed or solid in brain, incapable of accepting anything of fate after two months intoxication of youth and love, overwhelmed by all reveries of despair, had but one desire: to make speedy end of all.** **Emerged from Rue Plumet by boulevard, traversed Esplanade and bridge of Invalides, Champs-Élysées, Place Louis XV, reached Rue de Rivoli.** **Followed Rue Saint-Honoré through Passage Delorme; continued toward Halles.** **By circuit, reached Rue de la Poterie; near middle, came in contact with overturned wagon. Barricade begun there, abandoned.** **Left white omnibus horses behind.** **Received bullet wound near Rue du Contrat-Social.** **Reached elbow of Rue Mondétour, perceived light on pavement, bit of wine-shop, flickering lamp within shapeless wall, men crouching with guns on knees; all ten fathoms distant—interior of barricade.** **Raised eyes; splendid rectification effected in mind.** **Widening of sphere of thought peculiar to vicinity of grave makes one see clearly when near death. Vision of action he felt perhaps about to enter appeared no more lamentable but superb. War of street suddenly transfigured by unfathomable inward working of soul. All tumultuous interrogation points of reverie recurred in throngs without troubling him; he left none unanswered.** **Philosophy of duty**: Reflected on Colonel Pontmercy—father who had been proud soldier, guarded French frontier under Republic, touched Asia under Napoleon, beheld Genoa, Alexandria, Milan, Turin, Madrid, Vienna, Dresden, Berlin, Moscow, left drops of blood on victorious battlefields, grown gray in discipline and command, lived sword-belt buckled, epaulets on breast, cockade blackened with powder, brow furrowed with helmet, returned after twenty years with scarred cheek, smiling countenance, tranquil, admirable, pure as child, done everything for France, nothing against her. Reflected own day had come; must follow father, show himself brave, intrepid, bold, run to meet bullets, offer breast to bayonets, shed blood, seek enemy, seek death, wage civil war, descend to field of battle—the street. **Carries loaded pistols**: Took pistols Javert gave him at time of 3d February adventure; they remained loaded. **Questioning insurrection's validity**: As he meditated thus, dejected but resolute, hesitating in every direction, and shuddering at what he was about to do, his glance strayed to interior of barricade. Insurgents conversing in low voice, quasi-silence marking last stage of expectation.

## Father Gillenormand (evening 24th June 1832)
**Evening encounter**: Marius arrived at residence; Gillenormand grasped him at glance, found him noble and handsome. Upon learning girl's name related to Fauchelevent, declared absolutely: "Never, sir, never!"

**Sudden reversal and Marius's confession**: At tone of "never," Marius lost hope. Gillenormand seized him by collar, flung him into armchair with paternal warmth. **Marius passionately declared love for Cosette, described meeting her at Luxembourg, her father's planned departure to England, his desperation.** Stated: "She lives in a garden with an iron fence, in the Rue Plumet."

**Gillenormand's dangerous response and misrecognition**: **At words "Rue Plumet" Gillenormand interrupted his inhalation and allowed remainder of snuff to fall upon his knees.** **Delivered rambling response containing references to "Rue Blomet, Pamela, barracks, lancer," which passed before Marius like dissolving view.** **Terminated rambling in words Marius understood as mortal insult to Cosette: "make her your mistress."** **Those words entered heart of strict young man like sword.** Octogenarian raised hands to temples with anguish, recoiled, fell back into armchair, pulseless, voiceless, tearless. **However, Marius at age when one believes nothing evil. Suspicions are wrinkles; early youth has none. Gillenormand's dangerous mischaracterization left no trace in Marius's mind.**

## Café Corinthe and Barricade Construction (Evening 24th June 1832)
**Layout and history**: Ground floor with bar; first floor with billiard-table and wooden spiral staircase; cellar accessible via trap-door; second floor lodgings; two mansard attics. Originally _Pot-aux-Roses_; renamed _Corinthe_ after painter Natoire.

**Current proprietor and staff**: Widow Hucheloup continues wine-shop. Serving-maids: Matelote (large, plump, redhaired, noisy) and Gibelotte (tall, delicate, white, lymphatic pallor, languid, weary).

**Two barricades constructed**: Enjolras, Combeferre, Courfeyrac directed. Both resting on Corinthe house, forming right angle. Larger shut off Rue de la Chanvrerie; other closed Rue Mondétour on side of Rue de Cygne. **Interior: irregular square, closed on all sides, interval of twenty paces between grand barrier and lofty houses. Issue left free on Rue Mondétour opening through Rue des Prêcheurs into Halles.** Larger barricade: average height six or seven feet, stepped construction, outside composed of paling-stones, casks, wheels, omnibus pole upright with ropes, red flag fastened to pole floating over. Work completed in less than hour without single bear-skin cap appearing.

**Battle preparations and sentinels (evening 24th June)**: Forty-three insurgents including Enjolras, Combeferre, Courfeyrac, Bossuet, Joly, Bahorel, and Gavroche kneeling inside large barricade, heads on level with crest, guns and carbines aimed on stones as loop-holes, attentive, mute, ready to fire. Six commanded by Feuilly installed at windows of two stories of Corinthe with guns levelled. Terror seized street; all closed except wine-shop. Sentinels stationed: vidette of Rue de la Petite-Truanderie remained at post (nothing approaching from bridges and Halles direction). Two sentinels had fallen back. Enjolras and Combeferre seated near outlet of grand barricade, carbines in hand, listening for faintest sound of marching. Ten o'clock sounded from Saint-Merry.

## Javert Infiltration and Execution (Evening 24th June 1832)
**The arrest and revelation**: **Man of Rue des Billettes identified as Javert, Inspector of Police, aged fifty-two.** Seated at least-lighted table holding musket between legs. Enjolras hastily quitted Gavroche, murmured words; four broad-shouldered porters placed behind Javert's table.

**Documents found**: Little round card between glass pieces bearing arms of France and motto _Supervision and vigilance_; identified him as "JAVERT, inspector of police, aged fifty-two," signature of Prefect M. Gisquet. Also had watch and purse with gold pieces (undisturbed). Under watch in fob's bottom, found paper in envelope—five lines in handwriting of Prefect (content not yet revealed).

## Le Cabuc Execution and Enjolras's Justice (Evening 24th June 1832)
**Character**: Le Cabuc, utter stranger to insurgents, wearing threadbare street porter's jacket. Very drunk or assumed appearance. Examined large house at extremity of barricade commanding whole street, facing Rue Saint-Denis.

**Trial and execution by Enjolras**: **Enjolras, pale with bare neck and dishevelled hair, Greek-profile face, expression of wrath and chastity befitting Justice.** Never took eyes off Le Cabuc; allowed minute to pass, replaced watch in fob. Grasped Le Cabuc by hair as latter coiled into ball and shrieked; placed pistol muzzle to ear. Many intrepid men turned aside heads.

**Enjolras's justification speech**: "What that man did is frightful, what I have done is horrible. He killed, therefore I killed him. Insurrection must have discipline. Assassination is crime here more than elsewhere; we are priests of Republic, victims of duty, must not be slandered. I tried that man, condemned him to death. As for myself, constrained to do this, abhorring it, I judged myself also, you shall soon see to what I condemned myself." **Philosophy of necessity**: "One word more. In executing this man, I obeyed necessity; but necessity is monster of old world, necessity's name is Fatality. Law of progress is monsters shall disappear before angels, Fatality vanish before Fraternity. It is bad moment to pronounce word love. No matter, I pronounce it. I glorify it. Love, future is thine. Death, I use thee, but hate thee. Citizens, in future neither darkness nor thunderbolts; neither ferocious ignorance, nor bloody retaliation. As no Satan, no Michael. Future: no one kill anyone else, earth beam with radiance, human race love. Day will come, citizens, when all concord, harmony, light, joy, life; it will come, and in order that it may come we are about to die."

**Le Cabuc's true identity (police tradition)**: **Tradition of police (strange but probably well founded) states Le Cabuc was Claquesous. Dating from death of Le Cabuc, no longer any question of Claquesous. Claquesous left no trace of disappearance; would seem to have amalgamated himself with invisible. Life all shadows, end was night.**

## Gavroche and Others at Barricade (Evening 24th June 1832)
**Gavroche's activities**: Street child, homeless, hungry, clever pickpocket. Armed with pistol. Arrived at Rue du Pont-aux-Choux; attempted to purchase apple-turnover but had no money; picked up fallen lancer's horse; threw stone through hair-dresser's shop panes. Effected junction with Enjolras's band. Sang, whistled, hummed, ran ahead, pounded shutters with pistol butt. Completely carried away, radiant; undertaken to get everything in readiness. Everywhere at once. Enormous barricade felt him on its haunches.

**Laigle and Joly**: Laigle lived more with Joly than elsewhere. Morning of 5th June, Joly all stuffed up with catarrh beginning to spread to Laigle. Laigle's coat threadbare; Joly well dressed.

## M. Mabeuf's Heroic Sacrifice (Evening 24th June 1832)
**Destitution and joining**: Venerable old man of austerity and learning. **Final sacrifice (4th June)**: Sold unique copy of Diogenes Laertius, returned with one hundred francs. Seated himself on overturned post in garden at dawn, motionless.

**Evening 24th June—Passive withdrawal**: Encountered by band near Rue des Billettes. Set out to follow them. From that moment: uttered no word. Step suddenly became firm; artisans offered arms, refused with sign of head. Since arriving at Corinthe, no attention paid to him. Had not quitted mob; entered ground floor and seated himself behind counter. Retreated into himself. No longer seemed to look or think. Courfeyrac and others accosted him two or three times, warning of peril, beseeching withdrawal, but he did not hear. When not spoken to, his mouth moved as though replying to someone; when addressed, lips became motionless and eyes no longer appeared alive.

**During early battle hours**: Several hours before barricade attacked, assumed attitude which he did not afterwards abandon, with both fists planted on knees and head thrust forward as though gazing over precipice. Nothing moved him from this attitude; his mind did not seem in barricade. When each took position for combat, only single insurgent with naked sword watched over Javert in tap-room; Mabeuf remained there as well.

**Heroic emergence and death (moment of attack)**: At detonation, physical shock awakened him. Started up abruptly, crossed room, appeared on threshold of wine-shop at instant when Enjolras repeated appeal: "Does no one volunteer?" His presence produced sort of commotion in groups. Shout went up. Strode straight up to Enjolras; insurgents withdrew before him with religious fear. Tore flag from Enjolras, who recoiled in amazement. Since no one dared stop or assist him, this old man of eighty, with shaking head but firm foot, began slowly to ascend staircase of paving-stones arranged in barricade. **All around him cried: "Off with your hats!"** At every step mounted, it was frightful spectacle; his white locks, decrepit face, lofty bald wrinkled brow, amazed open mouth, aged arm upholding red banner, rose through gloom and were enlarged in bloody light of torch. Bystanders thought they beheld spectre of '93 emerging from earth with flag of terror in hand. **When he had reached last step, when this trembling terrible phantom, erect on pile of rubbish in presence of twelve hundred invisible guns, drew himself up in face of death as though more powerful than it, whole barricade assumed amid darkness a supernatural and colossal form.** **Enjolras's eulogy**: "Citizens! This is the example which the old give to the young. We hesitated, he came! We were drawing back, he advanced! This is what those who are trembling with age teach to those who tremble with fear! This aged man is august in the eyes of his country. He has had a long life and a magnificent death! Now, let us place the body under cover, that each one of us may defend this old man dead as he would his father living, and may his presence in our midst render the barricade impregnable!"

**The attack arrives**: Courfeyrac, Enjolras, Jean Prouvaire, Combeferre, Joly, Bahorel, Bossuet, and all rest ran tumultuously from wine-shop. It was almost too late. They saw glistening density of bayonets undulating above barricade. Municipal guards of lofty stature making their way in, some striding over omnibus, others through cut, thrusting before them the urchin, who retreated but did not flee.

**Unknown figures**: **Pale, thin, small, freckled, youthful artisan in tattered blouse and patched ribbed velvet trousers emerged from lodge, spoke to Courfeyrac in voice not in least womanly.** **Near Rue des Billettes, man of lofty stature, hair turning gray, bold and daring mien joined them.** Courfeyrac, Enjolras, Combeferre remarked him but none knew him. **At work on smaller barricade, making himself useful there. Young man who had been waiting for Courfeyrac at lodgings and inquired for M. Marius disappeared about time omnibus overturned.**
